correctness.rationale: Strict symmetrization uses Rayleigh extrema and the strictly positive simple minimum eigenvector of an irreducible Stieltjes matrix; the even/odd blocks yield the exact two extreme eigenvalues; monotonicity of the logarithmic derivative proves the unique fixed-budget scalar optimum; a strictly monotone boundary equation gives the unique budget threshold. The proof also establishes all limit laws. The standalone symbolic and numerical verifier passes; random trials are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Diagonal pinning with a fixed control budget is a natural numerical-conditioning problem for a four-site diffusion chain. This is the smallest path not isomorphic to a star; the two reflection parity sectors force a nontrivial tradeoff between extreme eigenvalues. The theorem gives a sharp active-site cutoff and globally unique allocations even against asymmetric controls, plus an explicit high-budget balancing law. These determine when interior controls are worth their cost, rather than merely rechecking an arbitrary fixed matrix.
